action: Poste Italiane customers: be wary of emails, calls or texts that use your name, contact details or contract information; do not share credentials.
date_note: Date of the forum post the article describes; Cybersecurity360 published November 19. Article gives the forum post as Tuesday 17 Nov and elsewhere as 18 Nov; not resolved.
exec: Customer contracts and contact details tied to a digital-signature service were reportedly leaked, raising phishing and fraud risk for customers of a major Italian provider.
plain: Poste Italiane told an Italian news site it had a data breach affecting a limited number of people, reported as over 1,500 customers. Names, emails and contract documents were reportedly exposed; Poste says payment credentials are safe.
summary: Cybersecurity360 reports that Poste Italiane confirmed a breach affecting a limited number of people. The 1,500 figure is the outlet's own; Poste gave no count. About 1 GB of files, which the outlet says appear tied to the PosteCert remote digital-signature service, include names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and contract documents. Poste is reported to say passwords and payment credentials are safe.
title: Poste Italiane confirms data breach; report puts it at over 1,500 customers

validation.note: Re-read Cybersecurity360 (19 Nov): the page does state a limited number of people, 1,500 customers (outlet's figure, not Poste's), PosteCert link, data types, passwords/payment safe, user flex22. Earlier review flag was mistaken; wording tightened so 1,500 is attributed to the outlet. Forum date 17 vs 18 Nov conflicts within the article. One search found no second publisher.

review.note: Cybersecurity360 page as read does not state the 1,500 figure (records_affected), a PosteCert link, a limited-number statement, that passwords and payment credentials are safe, or a Nov 17 forum post date.
